solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bodily parts in bears

definitions.meaning: to stomach something is to tolerate or bear it, so 'bears' is its third-person verb form

explanation.surface: A note on anatomy: the internal organs found inside a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bears' reads as about the animal, but 'bears' is the verb: he stomachs it, he bears it.
explanation.definitionFit: Organs of digestion are bodily parts; the verb sense means tolerates or puts up with.

clue.text: Middle of battle interrupted by little message

indicators.note: the middle pair is broken apart by a word placed between them
asks for the central letters of the word battle, its two middle letters

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for little

explanation.surface: A small dispatch arriving in the thick of a fight and breaking it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle of battle' gives the two Ts at its centre; WEE splits them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short post on the social network X, formerly Twitter: a brief online message.

clue.text: Silent relation

definitions.meaning: keeping ... means staying quiet, so ... is an adjective for silent

explanation.surface: A family member who says nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying nothing is to keep mum; a mother is a close kin member.

clue.text: Pain somewhere in the mountains with one getting cold

parts.note: a col is a pass or saddle between mountain peaks
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An ache suffered high in the mountains by a climber who has caught a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is a severe griping abdominal pain, especially in babies and horses.

clue.text: Class of Marines sorted out

indicators.note: letters sorted out are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A group of Marines in a class being organised.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small teaching group or class for discussion, often at university.

clue.text: Eastern fellow set about getting title

indicators.note: set about here means turned around, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man from the East starts out on acquiring a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name by which a book, film or song is known.

clue.text: One won't be able to understand characters in a book

definitions.text: One won't be able to understand characters in a book

parts.words: One won't be able to understand characters in a book
parts.note: the characters seem to be the people of a novel, but they are the printed letters an illiterate cannot make out

explanation.surface: Someone confused by the cast of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests a novel's cast; it means the printed letters themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot make sense of written letters is illiterate, a person unable to read.

clue.text: Slight fog starts to roll away over lake — there's a wind

parts.note: mist is a light fog

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A thin fog begins to drift off across a lake as the wind picks up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the start letters above L.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong cold northerly that blows down the Rhône valley into southern France.

clue.text: Piece of gym equipment making one smile

definitions.meaning: the ... is the balance ... used in gymnastics

explanation.surface: A gymnastics apparatus that makes a person grin.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasts perform on a narrow balance bar; to grin radiantly is also this word.

clue.text: Word of prayer when beset by minor physical disability

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: less means minor or smaller, as in a lesser matter
amen is the word that ends a prayer

explanation.surface: A prayer said over someone with a small physical ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Lameness is an impairment of the legs that makes walking difficult.

clue.text: Centaurs conjured up in an ancient civilisation

indicators.note: conjured suggests magic transforming the word, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Mythical horse-men summoned by magic in an old culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conjured up' rearranges CENTAURS. The answer is an adjective, as in 'an Etruscan', fitting 'in an ancient civilisation'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were a people of pre-Roman Italy whose culture flourished in Etruria.

clue.text: Crazy Greek character climbing — old and free from injury

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: mad means crazy
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
aged means old

explanation.surface: A mad Greek climber, elderly, comes through unhurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undamaged has suffered no harm, so it is intact.

clue.text: Listeners hear sounds? Only some

indicators.note: Only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about whether people listening pick up every noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Ears are the organs of hearing, punningly the parts that do the listening.

clue.text: Merchant taking around wine with skill

indicators.note: around signals turning the pieces round, reading them backwards

parts.note: red is red wine
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A dealer carting wine about, skilfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods, the work of a merchant.

clue.text: Pure art somehow bringing great joy

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Pure art producing ecstasy in the viewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is a feeling of intense delight or ecstasy.

clue.text: Bird ascended, everyone having turned up

parts.note: rose means went up, ascended

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means reversed, read from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A bird flew up and everybody showed up to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The rosella is a brightly coloured Australian parrot.

clue.text: Something full of holes presenting a problem?

definitions.meaning: a coarse sieve, full of holes
a puzzle or problem to work out

explanation.surface: Something riddled with holes causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse sieve for soil or gravel bears this name; so does a puzzling question.

clue.text: Wartime food plans suffering a setback

indicators.note: a setback sends the word backward, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: maps are plans, as of a building or town

explanation.surface: Wartime rationing schemes going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering a setback' reverses MAPS. SPAM, the tinned pork, was a staple in Britain during the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam, canned spiced ham, was a familiar ration in the 1940s.

clue.text: Vessel coming to area to dock

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A boat reaching a stretch of water to tie up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks nautical but is the verb meaning deduct, as in docking wages.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock pay is to deduct from it, take an amount away.

clue.text: Someone bending over in part of garden?

definitions.meaning: a shady leafy shelter in a garden

explanation.surface: A person stooping down in a corner of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafy arbour or shady retreat in a garden; also one who bows.

clue.text: Polite, like some servants?

definitions.meaning: ... servants are government administrative staff, so ... describes them

explanation.surface: Courteous, as servants are supposed to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Courteous behaviour is civil; government officials are civil servants.

clue.text: Cast provided with a humble dwelling

parts.note: to bung is informal British for to throw or cast
low means humble, of low rank

explanation.surface: A cast given a modest home, perhaps theatre actors on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' seems to be actors but is the verb throw, BUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey house, a type of home.

clue.text: Bird descended in America

definitions.meaning: a bird of the pigeon family
the American past tense of dive, where British usage has dived

explanation.surface: A bird landing in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon-like bird; in US English the past tense of dive, meaning plunged down.

clue.text: Edward oddly missing out as member of family

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Edward, strangely, being left out of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Dad is an informal word for father, a relative.

clue.text: The fellow given notice — and the boss giving it?

parts.note: he refers to the fellow
an ad, advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A man is sacked, and the one in charge was the one who sacked him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given notice' suggests dismissal; NOTICE is just AD, and the boss is the one who gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is the person in charge, such as a headteacher, the boss who would hand out the dismissal.

clue.text: Excellent leader trained dog

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A top-quality guide dog.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) gives AI; 'trained' rearranges LEADER into REDALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.
